data.content_ref: inline:The target conflates two distinct criteria into 'redundant probes of the same latent quality.' The verdict-shape's frontier-claim-honest criterion tests whether a candidate truthfully represents its own frontier status (an epistemic-integrity constraint), while the frontier-above-floor criterion tests whether the candidate exceeds a minimum threshold (a quality-minimum constraint). These are logically independent: a candidate can be honest about a low frontier (passing honesty, failing floor) or dishonest about a high frontier (passing floor, failing honesty). Calling them 'redundant' misrepresents the §11.3 structure, so the flag-sustained rationale is built on a false equivalence rather than a genuine assessment of the adjudication-ritual's criteria.
